definitions.explanation: Mochi that has been grilled or toasted, typically over a flame or in a toaster oven, causing it to puff up and develop a crispy exterior.
Jealousy, particularly the kind felt in romantic or close personal relationships. Often used in a somewhat lighthearted or teasing way.

examples.japanese: お{正月|しょうがつ}に{焼|や}き{餅|もち}を{焼|や}いた。
examples.english: I grilled mochi on New Year's.

examples.japanese: {醤油|しょうゆ}をつけた{焼|や}き{餅|もち}が{一番|いちばん}{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like grilled mochi with soy sauce the best.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}はすぐ{焼|や}き{餅|もち}を{焼|や}く。
そんなに{焼|や}き{餅|もち}を{焼|や}かないで、ただの{友達|ともだち}だよ。
examples.english: Don't be so jealous — we're just friends.

notes:
This word has two distinct meanings connected by a pun on the verb {焼|や}く (to grill/burn). Sense 1 is literal grilled mochi. Sense 2 uses the expression {焼|や}き{餅|もち}を{焼|や}く, which literally means "to grill grilled mochi" but idiomatically means "to be jealous."

USAGE:
The jealousy sense is most commonly used in the phrase {焼|や}き{餅|もち}を{焼|や}く. It tends to describe romantic jealousy and has a somewhat playful or teasing tone compared to the more serious {嫉妬|しっと}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焼|や}き{餅|もち}を{焼|や}く — to be jealous (sense 2); to grill mochi (sense 1)
- {焼|や}き{餅|もち}{焼|や}き — a jealous person
- {醤油|しょうゆ}{焼|や}き{餅|もち} — soy sauce grilled mochi

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {嫉妬|しっと} — jealousy (stronger, more serious)
- {妬|ねた}む — to envy, to be jealous of (verb)
- {羨|うらや}ましい — envious (less negative, more admiring)
